our_argument_summary: WIN-068 cites Kim & Chang (2018) Adv. Space Res. 61:2040-2049 as a retrospective 39-eclipse INTERMAGNET ensemble (1991-2016) whose perturbations are produced by the Chapman-Sq ionospheric mechanism (Chapman 1919; modern conductivity treatment Yamazaki & Maute 2017, SSR 206:299-405, DOI 10.1007/s11214-016-0282-z). We argue (1) the mechanism is non-discriminating — Chapman-Sq predicts the qualitative pattern without invoking dome geometry; (2) WIN-068 is post-hoc — Kim & Chang was published 2018, dome incorporated in V51.0 in early 2026 (~8-year gap); (3) WIN-068 attaches no dome-derived numerical prediction (FSF scaling enters only the WIN-010 2026 forward projection, not the 1991-2016 ensemble); (4) WIN-010 (2017 BOU), WIN-025 (2024 9-station), and WIN-068 (1991-2016 ensemble) triple-count the same Chapman-Sq mechanism at three aggregation scales. Verdict: Std Model Explains.

code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: Chapman (1919, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 218:1-118) is the founding Sq-mechanism paper, predating the dome by 107 years. Yamazaki & Maute (2017, SSR 206:299-405) provides the modern conductivity-tensor treatment. Eclipse-time ionospheric Sq disruption (UV ionization suppression -> E-region conductivity drop -> Y-component increase, X/Z/F decrease, 30-50 deg magnetic latitude peak, ~180 min window) is fully predicted by the standard framework. Dome adds no different numerical prediction for the ensemble.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: Kim & Chang (2018) published in Advances in Space Research vol 61 pp 2040-2049 (ISS-2747 closed-fixed verified the page-range and DOI 10.1016/j.asr.2018.02.003 family); dome model V51.0 incorporated this dataset in early 2026 (~8-year gap). code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: The 39-eclipse 1991-2016 ensemble attaches no dome-derived numerical prediction. The dome FSF scaling formula delta_Z = baseline * coverage * FSF (with FSF = H(r)/r reproducible at Pearson r ~= 0.9999 against the published values) is invoked only by the 2026 forward projection (WIN-010 territory), not by the Kim & Chang retrospective dataset. The ensemble statistical method derives its expected signal amplitude from the 1991-2016 data itself.

holes_found.description: finding factual error: "WIN-025 (9-station 2026 European cohort)" is wrong on both the year and continent. WIN-025 is the 2024 North American total solar eclipse (April 8, 2024), 9 INTERMAGNET stations, cited as Chernogor & Holub (2024) Adv. Space Res. DOI 10.1016/j.asr.2024.10.056. wins.json WIN-025.claim is "2024 eclipse 9-station magnetic" and WIN-025.detail_evidence states "April 8, 2024 total solar eclipse... during eclipse totality over North America (~15:00-21:00 UTC, April 8)". The "2026 European cohort" descriptor refers to the prospective FSF 9-station predictions cluster (E001-E009 family) discussed in WIN-010 forward-projection context, NOT to WIN-025. This appears in the finding (summary-table row), which is the field most readers see first — a dome defender can use this typo to discredit the cross-WIN triple-counting argument ("the reviewer cannot keep their own WINs straight, yet claims the dome conflates three eclipses").
holes_found.recommendation: Replace "(9-station 2026 European cohort)" with "(9-station 2024 North American cohort)" or "(9-station 2024 eclipse confirmation)" — both match WIN-025 wins.json and the Chernogor & Holub (2024) citation. Verify the analogous string in WIN-010.detail_evidence (current text: "WIN-025 already demonstrates for a confirmed 9-station European cohort (Chernogor & Holub, 2024)") and fix the same way — Chernogor & Holub (2024) is the 2024 North American eclipse paper, not a European cohort. See cross_win_consistency block below.

holes_found.description: finding wording: "the Chapman-Sq ionospheric framework... together with the Kim & Chang (2018) ensemble reproduces the 39-eclipse signal magnitude and geometry." The verb "reproduces" closes c16 H0 (good), but "magnitude and geometry" is a residual overclaim. Per our own detail_evidence (P3): "The Sq conductivity framework... predicts the qualitative pattern — Y-component increase, X/Z/F decrease, peak at eclipse maximum, strongest at Sq-vortex latitudes" — qualitative, not quantitative. Per detail_verdict_text (P2-P3): the ensemble amplitude comes from the 1991-2016 dataset itself, not from forward Chapman-Sq derivation. "Magnitude" attributes quantitative power to the framework that our own detail concedes does not exist a priori; the magnitude is in the empirical ensemble, not in the theory.
holes_found.recommendation: Soften "magnitude and geometry" to "qualitative ensemble pattern" or "component pattern, latitude dependence, and timescale" — or split: "the Chapman-Sq framework explains the ensemble geometry and the Kim & Chang (2018) ensemble supplies the empirical amplitudes; neither invokes dome cavity parameters." This keeps the non-discriminating verdict intact while removing the residual a-priori-magnitude overclaim. Carry severity minor since detail copy is already correct; this is a finding-only refinement.

stronger_arguments.description: The "Note: WIN-010/025/068 invoke the same Chapman-Sq mechanism at successive aggregation scales" addition in the finding (closing c16 H1) is the right structural move, but the rhetorical punch lands harder if the finding also names the in-sample-vs-out-of-sample asymmetry explicitly: WIN-068 is a retrospective citation of someone else dataset, WIN-025 is a post-hoc fit to data published five months before V51.0 incorporated it, only WIN-010 (2017 BOU) is plausibly prospective — and even WIN-010 uses the BOU 2017 magnitude as its 2026-projection anchor. The triple-counting collapses into a one-event-prospective-and-two-retrospective-restatements pattern that is much cleaner than "same mechanism three times." Could be added as one trailing sentence in finding or detail_verdict_text P5.

kernel_of_truth.description: Kim & Chang (2018) Adv. Space Res. 61:2040-2049 is a methodologically rigorous 39-eclipse INTERMAGNET ensemble (1991-2016) and the dome model is correctly citing it as observational evidence (data/wins.json WIN-068 detail_evidence P1). The dome does derive a station-to-station FSF scaling formula FSF = H(r)/r from its own geometry that reproduces the published values at Pearson r ~= 0.9999 (cross-verified at WIN-010 derives_from_dome=true on the scaling, c16 quantitative_verification block). And the gate-2 reasoning preserving the Std Model Explains verdict against the EXP-078 refraction-cascade objection (data/wins.json WIN-068 detail_extra, "added 2026-05 per ISS-1513") is conceptually correct: eclipse magnetic effects track apparent shadow geometry through line-of-sight UV interception, so the n(r) physical-altitude indeterminacy does not propagate into the magnetic-perturbation observable.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The genuine FSF derivation lives entirely on the WIN-010 2026 forward projection path; it never enters the 1991-2016 Kim & Chang ensemble counted as WIN-068 (data/wins.json WIN-068 detail_verdict_text P2: "FSF is not invoked anywhere in the 39-eclipse Kim & Chang (2018) ensemble evaluated in this WIN"). Recognizing a published ensemble in 2026 that was already published in 2018 is post-hoc literature citation, not prospective prediction. The Tier-1 Steelman admission in the dome own Evidence Ladder (data/wins.json WIN-068 detail_verdict_text P4) explicitly concedes WIN-068 alone cannot distinguish dome cavity dynamics from standard ionospheric physics — the dome itself classifies the eclipse magnetic evidence as non-discriminating. Counting WIN-010 + WIN-025 + WIN-068 as three separate confirmed predictions for the same Chapman-Sq mechanism (single-station 2017 BOU + 9-station 2024 + 39-eclipse 1991-2016 ensemble) inflates the score without adding independent evidence.

advocate_mode.best_defense: A capable dome defender attacks on two parallel fronts. First, on facts: "Your finding says WIN-025 is a 9-station 2026 European cohort. WIN-025 in your own wins.json is the 2024 North American eclipse cited from Chernogor & Holub (2024). If you cannot keep your own three WINs straight, your central triple-counting claim — that we are double-counting WIN-010/025/068 — is rhetorically gutted: a reviewer who confuses 2024 North America with 2026 Europe is not in a position to police our aggregation discipline. The same wrong descriptor also appears in your WIN-010 detail_evidence, so this is not a typo — it is a systematic confusion between our 2024 retrospective WIN-025 and our 2026 prospective cohort that you yourselves quantitatively verified at Pearson r ~= 0.9999 (and credited as a genuine dome-derived FSF scaling). Second, on framing: your finding now says the Chapman-Sq framework reproduces the 39-eclipse signal magnitude AND geometry. But your own detail evidence concedes Sq predicts only the qualitative pattern, and the ensemble magnitudes come from the 1991-2016 dataset itself. So you have replaced one overclaim (the dome predicts WIN-068) with a different overclaim (Sq predicts WIN-068 magnitudes). That is symmetric: neither model derives the magnitudes a priori; both rely on independently-measured inputs. The non-discriminating verdict survives, but the rhetorical claim that Sq beats the dome on a-priori derivability does not survive your own qualitative-pattern concession."
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Patch the WIN-025 descriptor in WIN-068 finding (and the parallel string in WIN-010 detail_evidence) before any defender screenshot circulates. The factual fix is one-line ("2024 North American" replacing "2026 European"). For the magnitude/geometry framing, replace "reproduces the 39-eclipse signal magnitude and geometry" with "explains the ensemble pattern (component signs, latitude peak, ~180-min timescale) using independently-measured ionospheric inputs" — that keeps the non-discriminating verdict intact while preempting the symmetric-overclaim attack. Defense rating 4/5 because both fronts can land in a single screenshot of the finding alone, and the factual error compounds the framing critique.

cross_win_consistency.inconsistencies_found: WIN-010 detail_evidence carries the same "2026 European" mis-attribution to WIN-025/Chernogor & Holub 2024: "as WIN-025 already demonstrates for a confirmed 9-station European cohort (Chernogor & Holub, 2024)". WIN-025 itself (data/wins.json WIN-025) claims "2024 eclipse 9-station magnetic" and cites Chernogor & Holub (2024) Adv. Space Res. DOI 10.1016/j.asr.2024.10.056 for the April 8, 2024 total solar eclipse over North America (15:00-21:00 UTC). The same factual error appearing in two WIN bodies (WIN-068 finding + WIN-010 detail_evidence) suggests a copy-paste cascade from a common pre-V51 draft, NOT independent slips. WIN-010 detail_verdict_text legitimately discusses the "nine-station 2026 European cohort" — but that refers to the FSF Pearson r ~= 0.991/0.994 forward-projection analysis (E001-E009 family), a different cohort from the 2024 Chernogor & Holub observation that anchors WIN-025. The dome defender attack vector is the rhetorical inconsistency: we triple-count-shame the dome for conflating three eclipses while our own prose conflates a 2024 retrospective and a 2026 prospective into a single "European cohort." A WIN-010 follow-up review (c14 or queue push) should patch the detail_evidence string and verify no third occurrence exists in SEC-* prose.
